name: folio

scripts.pages:build: VITE_BASE=/folio/ npm run build && node tools/stamp-sw.mjs dist
scripts.author: node --experimental-strip-types tools/authoring/cli.ts
scripts.coverage:all: mkdir -p .coverage && npm run coverage:unit >.coverage/unit.log 2>&1 && npm run e2e 2>&1 | tee .coverage/e2e.log && node tools/coverage-report.mjs --per-file

comment:coverage-combined: Combined coverage measured 97.87-97.92% over six runs (2026-10-31): five on the dev box and one in CI. It then rose to 98.00-98.04% once the e2e collected uncaught errors properly and three vacuous assertions were replaced with real ones. Floor is 97.5: 0.35pp below the lowest figure ever observed (97.85) and about 1.7x the measured 0.21pp band. The margin is deliberate and larger than the 0.06pp the old floor used: CON-COV-002 forbids lowering a floor, so an over-tight one has to be walked back and an over-loose one merely ratchets again. Drift, measured rather than inferred: the COMBINED figure has been observed between 97.85% and 98.06% across twelve runs (ten here, two in CI) — a 0.21pp band, about 18 lines of 8807. Underneath it the BROWSER half swings far more, 3965-4089 covered lines over six runs, because a session that renders slightly differently or a check that retries moves a hundred lines; most of that is absorbed by the union, since the unit half already covers those lines. src/shader.ts itself varies by three lines (150-153). An earlier version of this note said the three-line shader figure WAS the drift, which inferred the whole from one file (CON-DATA-001) — and it is the number the headroom argument rests on. The thing that USED to drift — destroy() and the webglcontextlost handler, 13 lines, once in three runs — is deterministic now: the e2e fires WEBGL_lose_context.loseContext() rather than hoping a page detaches the canvas before closing. The recorded cause for that swing (headless Chrome refusing a WebGL context) was wrong; a probe granted one 9 times out of 9. Never raise this on a single run.
comment:coverage-logs: coverage:all TEES the e2e output — it is both printed and kept at .coverage/e2e.log. It used to go to /dev/null, so a failing e2e inside a coverage run stopped the chain saying only "1 check(s) failed". The first fix redirected it to a file instead, which was WORSE in CI: .coverage is gitignored, ci.yml uploads only *.lcov, and the runner workspace is discarded — so the one place the output was still visible (stderr on the terminal) stopped being visible too. tee keeps both.
comment:coverage-floor: coverage:gate hardcodes the floor rather than relying on `npm run X -- --min N`. The passthrough is npm-version dependent: it applied in CI and silently did NOT apply locally, which would have left the gate unable to fail after an npm upgrade. Hardcode, like test:gate.
comment:coverage: test:gate floors are a RATCHET — raise them in the PR that earns the improvement, never lower them to make a build green (CON-COV-002). These are the UNIT-only floors; the combined floor lives in coverage:gate and is documented above. Baseline 38.91/74.52/39.41 set 2026-09-20 when import-all first forced the whole of src/ into the denominator (the previously reported 87.65% measured only five files). Phase 1 raised it to 86.05/71.67/75.42 — branches fell because newly-covered files brought their unexercised branches into the denominator, which is the honest direction. Ratcheted again 2026-10-31 to 95.5/89/80 from three runs measuring 95.99 lines, 89.62 functions and 80.39-80.41 branches; the floors had been left at 85/75/71 with eleven points of slack, in the very change that rewrote this note to say floors are a ratchet. This field used to say "Destination is 95" and "remaining climb to 95 needs browser-side coverage (shader/engine/tilt)": both were left standing after the combined floor passed 95 and reached 97.5, so the record contradicted the gate it describes — the same stale-note failure task 14c was closed for.
comment:author: The AI authoring pipeline (npm run author) needs @anthropic-ai/sdk. Install it on demand — `npm i -D @anthropic-ai/sdk` — it is not part of the app build.
